title: Pause before standing from a chair
summary: An invented everyday-activity record that keeps directions and inhibition separate from joint motion.

joint_actions.action: maintain an unforced relationship to the upper spine
incline the trunk as one coordinated action

instruction.activity: Beginning to stand from an ordinary chair.

directions.cue: Allow length and width without arranging a fixed posture.
Let the whole torso incline rather than pulling the head backward.

instruction.inhibition: Pause before carrying out the habitual first effort; the pause is not a command to freeze.
instruction.manual_guidance_boundary: Hands-on guidance is part of the source practice and is not represented or replaced by this visualization.

variations.note: Use a higher chair so the everyday activity requires less effort.

cautions: Use stable support and do not attempt the standing phase if balance is uncertain.
safety.notes: The page cannot reproduce a teacher's observation or manual guidance.

source.tradition_basis: Project-authored description informed by general Alexander Technique concepts of activity, direction, and inhibition; no teacher text was copied.
source.rights_basis: provisional: project-authored description with an explicit boundary around manual teaching

review.notes: Requires review by an Alexander Technique practitioner.
